title: doctor's hook-carrier advisory carries the AT-grammar remedy text
body:
`intent doctor --verbose` attaches the AT-grammar remedy text to the hook-carrier advisory. The detection is right and the remedy is prose about acceptance-test rows, on a subject that has none.

FAMILY: one of three where a reporter reads the CARRIER and expects the GATE BODY's properties. Fixing this one does not close the other two -- see the shim-reads-STALE and gate-not-running issues.

MEASURED, first-hand, read-only in the Intent tree, `intent doctor --verbose`, rc=0, a 7-line report holding exactly one finding (pairing control: 1):

  advisory: .githooks/pre-commit.intent -- advisory -- the hook carrier is 25609 byte(s) and the
  template in the resolved install is 34701 -- the carrier is a copy taken at install time and
  nothing re-copies it, so the guards it runs are the generation it was installed with. Reported
  and NOT counted: measured across the fleet this is true of every estate, and a finding that is
  permanently true everywhere is one nobody reads
    remedy: nothing is owed now: the row is well-formed and resolves. Rewrite it in the v3 grammar
    when the thread is next touched; a closed thread carries it as it is

"Rewrite it in the v3 grammar when the thread is next touched" is the remedy for a legacy AT reference. A hook carrier is not a thread, is not touched, and has no grammar. In Conflab the same reporter emits AT-grammar remedies against `intent/.canon/st/ST0121.json` AT rows, where the text is correct -- so this is one remedy string reused across two subjects, not a wrong string.

THE ADVISORY'S OWN DETECTION IS GOOD AND SHOULD NOT BE LOST IN THE FIX: it explains why it is not counted -- permanently true in every estate, and a finding that is always true is one nobody reads. That reasoning is worth keeping; only the remedy is wrong.

FALSIFIER: run `intent doctor --verbose` in an estate whose carrier byte-size differs from the resolved template. If the remedy on the carrier advisory names the carrier, the install, or the copy -- anything but rewriting a row in the v3 grammar -- this is fixed or was never present.

PROVENANCE: sighted by hv ~12:00Z and routed via intent-vc; placed and re-derived first-hand by intent-dc. NOT reproducible in Conflab post-hop, because Conflab's carrier is now the shim and Intent's is still the install-time copy -- a different subject in the same reporter.
